extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newsroom editors, reporters and news organizations adopting solutions/constructive journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Producing news stories that foreground credible responses to social problems, explaining how they work, assessing evidence of effectiveness, and acknowledging limits while preserving critical reporting and complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place possible solutions front and center
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on the response to the problem; put possible solutions at the heart of the story rather than only describing the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes solutions journalism from standard problem-only coverage; used by Solutions Journalism Network to separate quality solutions reporting from mere PR or boosterism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine how the solution works
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the mechanism, evidence, and process by which the solution produces results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the workflow, actors, implementation steps, causal mechanisms and practical details so readers understand why and how an intervention produces outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide evidence of effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Show data or results demonstrating whether the solution achieved its intended outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quantitative and qualitative evidence, outcomes data, evaluations, citations — not just assertions — to substantiate claims of effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify what the solution cannot do and under what conditions it might fail or be inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include caveats, boundary conditions, trade-offs and unanswered questions to avoid overclaiming and to help assess replicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future-oriented framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask 'To what end?' and 'Where to?' rather than only 'Why?' or 'From where?'; orient stories toward consequences and possible futures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on trajectories, next steps, and implications for the future rather than solely diagnosing past or present problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solutions-focused (credible solutions, not just problems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Center reporting on credible responses and constructive initiatives rather than repeatedly emphasizing problems without responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure solutions are realistic and evidence-based rather than aspirational wish-listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage diverse perspectives constructively in coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult and represent multiple stakeholders, including those affected, implementers, critics, and experts to avoid one-sided portrayals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement over outrage
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize reporting that invites civic engagement and constructive response rather than stoking anger or outrage for its own sake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use story forms and tone aimed at motivating informed action and deliberation rather than polarizing reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness over good intentions
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate initiatives by actual outcomes and measurable impact rather than by the sincerity of actors' intentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess programs on evidence and results, not on whether participants 'meant well.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Complementary to critical reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive journalism should complement—and not replace—traditional critical, watchdog reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain investigative rigor and hold power to account while also covering solutions; avoid turning constructive approaches into uncritical promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid positivity-for-its-own-sake / PR / boosterism
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not produce mere 'good news' boosterism, PR, advocacy, or cheerleading for institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive reporting should not shy away from critique; avoid stories that feel promotional, single-organization spotlights, or uncritical celebrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communities solving local problems (newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories showing communities actively solving local problems qualify as solutions-focused news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize local context, actors, processes and lessons that could inform other communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies that worked elsewhere (newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of policies implemented elsewhere that produced positive outcomes and could be informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify transferability conditions and evidence supporting the policy's success in its original context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Movements producing change (newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on movements that have demonstrable impact or produced concrete change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document mechanisms of change, scale, and implications for broader practice or policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual actions with broader impact (newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Profiles of individuals whose actions led to broader, replicable effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link individual initiatives to systems-level lessons or potential scale-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation in service delivery (newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories about new or improved ways of delivering public or social services that yield better outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain operational changes, implementation challenges, and measured benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restorative responses to harm (newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of restorative justice, repair, or remediation efforts following harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess outcomes for victims, communities and systems; avoid glossing over unresolved issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation efforts (newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on reconciliation processes that address historical or interpersonal harm and produce measurable progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include multiple perspectives, metrics of progress, and acknowledgments of remaining limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replicable models (newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that document models which can be replicated elsewhere with attention to context and constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on necessary conditions, adaptations, and evidence that supports transferability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pure feel-good without substance
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't publish stories that are only emotionally uplifting but lack substantive evidence or broader relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require outcomes, mechanisms or lessons that justify editorial space beyond transient uplift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid PR campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject stories that are essentially marketing or promotional material from organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vet sources, disclose conflicts of interest, and seek independent verification rather than republishing organizational messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid single-organization promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Be cautious of profiles or pieces that primarily serve to promote one organization without critical assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualize the organization within a broader field, include independent perspectives and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject unverified claims of effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't treat unproven or unverified assertions of success as fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require documentation, data, or independent evaluation before presenting effectiveness claims as established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid aspirational-but-unacted-upon solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that are merely aspirational without concrete action or implementation should not be presented as solutions journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between proposals/ideas and implemented interventions with evidence of outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-base for solution claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A robust evidence-base should underpin claims about a solution's success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use empirical data, evaluations, measurable outcomes and sources that corroborate claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replicability assessed
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether and how a solution can be reproduced in other contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify contextual factors, necessary resources, and adaptations required for replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations acknowledged (quality marker)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state limits, uncertainties and boundary conditions of the solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include discussion of failure modes, unknowns, and where the approach may not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple stakeholders consulted
rubrics_metrics.description: Include perspectives from diverse stakeholders, including beneficiaries, implementers, critics and independent experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid single-source narratives; triangulate claims using varied viewpoints and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain complexity (avoid oversimplification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not over-simplify causal chains or present neat success stories that omit nuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve system complexity, trade-offs and unintended consequences in reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track long-term outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider and report on long-term results rather than only immediate or short-term indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, follow-up on earlier interventions and report on sustained impact or relapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss failures as well as successes
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on what didn't work together with successes to provide a realistic and useful evidence base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including failures helps audiences assess risk, context, and learning for replication.
